questions.statement: Choose the correct form to complete the sentence: The letter ___ every morning.
questions.context: Every morning the same delivery arrives at the office.

options.feedback: Correct. The present simple passive is formed with is or are plus the past participle, so is delivered is right.
Incorrect. Delivers is active present simple, but the letter cannot deliver itself.
Incorrect. Is delivering is present continuous active, which describes an action in progress, not a daily routine.
Incorrect. Delivered alone is past simple active; the passive needs the auxiliary is before the participle.

questions.explanation:
The present simple passive uses am, is or are plus the past participle. The letter receives the action, so we write is delivered every morning.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence with the correct passive form: The bridge ___ in 1990.
questions.context: A local newspaper reported the history of the town.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Built is active past simple and would mean the bridge did the building.
Correct. The past simple passive is was or were plus the past participle, so was built fits the year 1990.
Incorrect. Is built is present simple passive and clashes with the finished past time in 1990.
Incorrect. Builds is active present simple and describes a routine, not a past event.

questions.explanation:
A finished past action in the passive takes was or were plus the past participle, as in the bridge was built in 1990.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which form correctly completes the sentence? The house ___ at the moment.
questions.context: The painters are still working on the old house.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Is painting is active; it would mean the house is applying paint itself.
Incorrect. Paints is active present simple and shows a habit, not an action happening now.
Correct. The present continuous passive is is or are being plus the past participle, so is being painted describes work in progress.
Incorrect. Has painted is active present perfect and does not express the ongoing action.

questions.explanation:
To show an action in progress that is done to the subject, use is or are being plus the past participle.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: The road ___ when we arrived.
questions.context: We reached the town while the workers were fixing the main road.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Was repairing is active and means the road was fixing something.
Incorrect. Repaired is active past simple; it loses the idea of an action in progress.
Incorrect. Is repaired is present passive and does not match the past moment when we arrived.
Correct. The past continuous passive is was or were being plus the past participle, so was being repaired shows the ongoing action.

questions.explanation:
An ongoing past action done to the subject takes was or were being plus the past participle.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence with the correct form: The report ___ yet.
questions.context: The manager is waiting for the monthly report.

options.feedback: Correct. The present perfect passive is has or have been plus the past participle, so has not been finished is right.
Incorrect. Has not finished is active and suggests the report finished something by itself.
Incorrect. Is not finishing is active present continuous and ignores the link to now.
Incorrect. Did not finish is active past simple and drops the passive auxiliary been.

questions.explanation:
The present perfect passive links a past action to now with has or have been plus the past participle.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: The tickets ___ before we got there.
questions.context: We arrived late at the box office last night.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Had sold is active and would mean the tickets sold something themselves.
Correct. The past perfect passive is had been plus the past participle, so had been sold marks the earlier past event.
Incorrect. Were selling is active past continuous and does not show the action was completed first.
Incorrect. Have sold is active present perfect and does not fit a past before another past.

questions.explanation:
The past perfect passive uses had been plus the past participle for an action completed before another past moment.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct form: The results ___ tomorrow.
questions.context: The judges are still deciding on the competition entries.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Will announce is active future and would mean the results announce something.
Incorrect. Are announcing is active present continuous and does not express a future action in the passive.
Correct. The future simple passive is will be plus the past participle, so will be announced is right.
Incorrect. Announced is active past simple and clashes with tomorrow.

questions.explanation:
The future simple passive is will be plus the past participle for an action that will happen to the subject.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: By next year the project ___ .
questions.context: The construction company is working to a fixed schedule.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Will have completed is active and means the project completes something else.
Incorrect. Will be completing is active future continuous and loses the passive sense.
Incorrect. Has completed is active present perfect and cannot follow by next year.
Correct. The future perfect passive is will have been plus the past participle, so will have been completed fits by next year.

questions.explanation:
The future perfect passive uses will have been plus the past participle for an action finished before a future time.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: This form ___ by the manager.
questions.context: The company has a strict procedure for official documents.

options.feedback: Correct. After a modal the passive is be plus the past participle, so must be signed is the right form.
Incorrect. Must sign is active; it would mean the form signs something.
Incorrect. Must is followed by the bare infinitive, so must signing is not grammatical.
Incorrect. Have must be followed by the past participle signed, not the noun sign.

questions.explanation:
Modal verbs form the passive with be plus the past participle, as in must be signed.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is the correct passive form of Shakespeare wrote Hamlet?
questions.context: A teacher is explaining how to change an active sentence into the passive.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Wrote is the past simple, but the passive needs the past participle written.
Correct. The past simple passive needs was or were plus the past participle written, and the agent follows by.
Incorrect. Is written is present passive and changes the tense of the original.
Incorrect. Wrote is active and leaves the sentence without the passive auxiliary was.

questions.explanation:
To turn an active past simple into the passive, use was or were plus the past participle and add by before the agent.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct passive transformation of They have repaired the car.
questions.context: A mechanic has just finished working on the family car.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is active present perfect and misses the passive auxiliary been.
Incorrect. Is repairing is active present continuous and changes the tense.
Correct. The present perfect passive is has been plus the past participle, so The car has been repaired is right.
Incorrect. Was repairing is active past continuous and changes both tense and voice.

questions.explanation:
Transforming a present perfect active sentence into the passive keeps has or have and adds been before the past participle.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which tense and voice is used in The cake was being baked?
questions.context: A student is analysing the form of a sentence in a grammar exercise.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The past simple passive would be was baked, without being.
Incorrect. The present continuous passive would be is being baked.
Incorrect. The past perfect passive would be had been baked.
Correct. Was being plus the past participle is the past continuous passive, an action in progress in the past.

questions.explanation:
Was being baked combines the past auxiliary was, the continuous being and the participle baked, so it is the past continuous passive.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
questions.context: A student must choose the sentence that contains no grammar error.

options.text: The window was broken by the storm.
options.feedback: Correct. The passive uses was plus the past participle broken, and by introduces the agent.

options.text: The window was broke by the storm.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Broke is the past simple, but the passive requires the participle broken.

options.text: The window did broken by the storm.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Did cannot introduce a passive; the auxiliary must be was.

options.text: The window was break by the storm.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Break is the base form and cannot follow the auxiliary was.

questions.explanation:
The past simple passive is was or were plus the past participle, so broken is the only form that fits.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: She hopes ___ to the party.
questions.context: The club organises a big party every December.

options.feedback: Incorrect. To invite is active and means she will invite someone else.
Correct. The passive infinitive is to be plus the past participle, so to be invited is right.
Incorrect. To be inviting is a continuous active form, not a passive infinitive.
Incorrect. Inviting is a gerund and does not follow hopes in this structure.

questions.explanation:
The passive infinitive is formed with to be plus the past participle, as in to be invited.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: He hates ___ .
questions.context: A speaker dislikes it when other people cut in while talking.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Interrupting is active and means he interrupts other people.
Incorrect. The infinitive needs the participle interrupted, not the base form interrupt.
Correct. After hate the passive gerund is being plus the past participle, so being interrupted is right.
Incorrect. Interrupt is a bare verb and cannot stand after hates in this meaning.

questions.explanation:
The passive gerund is being plus the past participle, so he hates being interrupted means others interrupt him.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: The window ___ by the children.
questions.context: A mother is trying to explain the damage to a neighbour.

options.feedback: Incorrect. This is active and would mean the window broke something.
Incorrect. This is active continuous and does not express a completed past action.
Incorrect. After might the verb needs the bare infinitive, so broke cannot follow it.
Correct. A modal perfect passive is modal plus have been plus the past participle, so might have been broken is right.

questions.explanation:
A modal perfect passive combines the modal, have, been and the past participle to show a possible past action.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the question: ___ the letters sent yesterday?
questions.context: A secretary is checking whether the letters left the office yesterday.

options.feedback: Correct. Were forms the past simple passive question together with the past participle sent.
Incorrect. Did would create the active question Did the letters send, which is not passive.
Incorrect. Are forms a present passive question and clashes with yesterday.
Incorrect. Have would need the past participle been, as in have the letters been sent.

questions.explanation:
A past simple passive question begins with was or were and keeps the past participle sent.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: The email ___ by the assistant.
questions.context: An assistant forgot to send an important email.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Send is the base form; the passive needs the participle sent.
Correct. The negative past simple passive is was not plus the past participle, so was not sent is right.
Incorrect. Did not is active and must be followed by the base form, not sent.
Incorrect. The sentence lacks the auxiliary was, so it is not a complete passive.

questions.explanation:
To make a past simple passive negative, put not after was or were and keep the past participle.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: The song ___ by millions of people this week.
questions.context: The same popular song is playing in many shops this week.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Sang is the past simple, but the passive needs the participle sung.
Incorrect. Is singing is active and means the song sings by itself.
Correct. The present continuous passive is is being plus the past participle sung, so is being sung is right.
Incorrect. The words are in the wrong order; being must come before sung.

questions.explanation:
The present continuous passive puts is or are being before the past participle, as in is being sung.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is active, not passive?
questions.context: A teacher asks the class to spot the sentence that is not in the passive voice.

options.text: The meal was prepared by the chef.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Was prepared plus the agent by the chef makes this a passive sentence.
Incorrect. Has been prepared is the present perfect passive.
Incorrect. Is being prepared is the present continuous passive.
Correct. The chef prepared the meal is active because the subject chef performs the action.

questions.explanation:
A sentence is active when the subject performs the action, so the chef prepared the meal is active while the others are passive.
---
questions.subject: ingles
